varieties.name: Nantes type
varieties.note: Kept from the existing crop-catalog.ts entry — this pass confirms and sharpens it below with Sakata's own Scarlet Nantes page, which restricts a Nantes-type carrot to cool-season growing specifically (not truly 'either season' as the catalog's original note implies).

varieties.name: Allyance F1 (or similar season-tuned hybrid)
varieties.note: Kept from the existing crop-catalog.ts entry — not independently re-verified in this pass.

varieties.name: Chantenay Karoo
varieties.season: Frost-free, warmer growing conditions; associated by name with the Karoo
varieties.traits: Short, broad-shouldered, conical root; good for heavier/shallower soils; heat tolerant
varieties.note: Its Sakata name and description directly tie it to hot, frost-free conditions — the best-sourced fit for the Karoo and other hot zones among the carrots checked in this pass.

evidence.quote: Chantenay Karoo is a short, broad-shouldered, conical-rooted carrot bred for frost-free, warmer growing conditions... well suited to heavier soils.
evidence.doc: Chantenay Karoo, Sakata product page (fetched directly, verbatim)

varieties.name: Kuroda
varieties.traits: Long, wedge-shaped, deep orange root; heat-tolerant Japanese type; widely grown in warmer regions of SA and the tropics
varieties.note: Sakata's own description restricts Kuroda to warm-season growing, unlike the Nantes/Scarlet Nantes types below which are restricted the other way (cool-season) — this is the clearest hot/cold split found for carrots in this pass.

evidence.quote: Kuroda is a warm season carrot, producing a long, wedge-shaped root with a deep orange colour... popular in tropical and sub-tropical growing regions.
evidence.doc: Kuroda, Sakata product page (fetched directly, verbatim)

varieties.name: Scarlet Nantes
varieties.traits: Cylindrical, blunt-tipped, smooth, sweet, coreless; classic Nantes type
varieties.note: The classic Nantes-type, seed-saveable OP carrot, explicitly restricted by Sakata to cool-season growing — the direct opposite constraint to Kuroda above, and the source this file uses to sharpen the existing catalog's generic 'Nantes type / either season' entry.

evidence.quote: Scarlet Nantes is a cool season carrot variety producing cylindrical, blunt-tipped roots with a smooth skin and sweet flavour.
evidence.doc: Scarlet Nantes, Sakata product page (fetched directly, verbatim)

karoo-arid.text: Hot, frost-free interior — Chantenay Karoo (by name and description) and Kuroda (explicitly a warm-season type) are the two best-sourced fits; the classic Nantes/Scarlet Nantes types are a cool-season crop here, sown for a cooler window rather than mid-summer.

lowveld-bushveld.text: Hot, frost-free — same warm-season logic as karoo-arid: Kuroda and Chantenay Karoo are the sourced fits; Scarlet Nantes should be timed to the cooler months.

subtropical-coast.text: Warm, frost-free coast — Kuroda and Chantenay Karoo again fit the warm-season description; Scarlet Nantes needs a cooler-month sowing window here too.

highveld.text: Cool to cold interior — Scarlet Nantes' cool-season description fits the highveld's climate for most of the growing calendar.

midlands-mistbelt.text: Cool, high-rainfall — Scarlet Nantes' cool-season description is a good match.

high-mountain.text: Cold, short season — Scarlet Nantes' cool-season description fits, though no source addresses frost tolerance specifically for this zone.

western-cape.text: Winter-rainfall, cool-to-mild — Scarlet Nantes' cool-season description fits the Mediterranean climate.

southern-cape.text: Mild, year-round rainfall — Scarlet Nantes' cool-season description is the closer fit of the two Sakata types checked.

gaps: No source was found giving carrot varieties specifically for the Karoo, lowveld, or coastal zones beyond the general 'warm-season' vs 'cool-season' distinction Sakata gives on its own product pages — the zoneAdvice above extrapolates that hot/cold split onto the 8 named zones rather than citing a zone-specific SA trial or guide.
Maturity days-to-harvest were not stated by Sakata for any of the three new varieties, so 'maturity' is left as a coarse early/medium/late judgement rather than a sourced number.
The existing catalog's Allyance F1 entry was not independently re-verified — no product page for it was found/opened in this pass.
